title: More Describing Words
description: Describing people, places and situations the way Indonesians do: busy or quiet, easy or a hassle, friendly, cute, handsome, safe, refreshing.

items.registerNotes: Casually rame. Usually a good thing, busy and fun: a ramai warung is a popular one. Noisy in a bad way is berisik.
The opposite of ramai: an empty street, a shop with no customers. It can feel a little lonely or eerie, unlike tenang (calm, peaceful).
For places, chairs and situations: Kamarnya nyaman. Casually enak covers this too: Enak tempatnya.
Casual, but everyone says it: Ribet banget urusannya (The paperwork's such a hassle). Of a person, it means fussy. Neutral words are rumit and repot.
The everyday word; mudah means the same in writing and formal speech. Gampang, kok (It's easy, honestly) reassures someone.
Sulit is the more formal word. Susah is also hardship: hidup susah (a hard life).
Careful saying it about food you're served or someone's home; unik (unusual, special) is the kinder word.

items.pitfallNote: Lucu covers both funny and cute: Anaknya lucu means the child is cute, not that they tell jokes.

items.registerNotes: For women, and for pretty things like a dress or a garden. Men are ganteng, and scenery is usually indah.
The everyday word; tampan is formal.
items.cultureNote: Looks are commented on openly: being told you're ganteng, or that you've put on weight (gemuk), are both ordinary small talk and not meant as rude.

items.registerNotes: Orangnya ramah (They're really friendly) is a common compliment. It's also in ramah lingkungan (environmentally friendly).
Also a joking complaint to a friend who's been out of touch: Sombong, nih, nggak pernah kabar.
A warm compliment, also for doing something regularly: Rajin olahraga, ya. The opposite is malas.
Casually males, and it's more 'can't be bothered' than lazy: Males ah, hujan (Can't be bothered, it's raining).
Casually pinter. Before an activity it praises a skill: pintar masak (a good cook).
items.cultureNote: Learners get praised a lot: Pintar bahasa Indonesia, ya. A modest Masih belajar (I'm still learning) is the usual reply.
Modesty is valued: hosts call their home or meal sederhana or seadanya (just what we have), however good it is. A compliment is the right reply.

items.registerNotes: For roads, rooms and clothes: jalannya sempit (the road's narrow), celananya sempit (the trousers are tight).
For area: a spacious room or a wide stretch of land is luas, while besar is size in general. Kamarnya luas (The room's spacious).
From kenal (to know someone). Famous for something takes dengan: Warung ini terkenal dengan sotonya.
Yang penting… (The main thing is…) sums things up: Yang penting sehat (As long as you're healthy).
Casually just bahaya, which is also 'danger' on warning signs.
Casually it also means all fine, no problem: Aman? Aman. (All good? All good.)
Casually seger. A cold drink, fruit, a shower or cool morning air can all be segar.

items.cultureNote: Dress sopan, with shoulders and knees covered, for mosques, temples and visiting families.

items.registerNotes: Santai saja (Take it easy, no rush) is what people say to put you at ease.
